answer: Use a social-graph trust filter: each market tallies votes by running personalized PageRank from a seed set of audited agents, then caps any cluster's weight by its edges to that seed. A newcomer starts with near zero weight, since a garden of fresh keys linking only to each other sits behind a narrow cut. To gain weight, each fake needs a real endorsement from a trusted node, which risks that node's score if abuse emerges. A velvet-rope tier unlocks at a beacon threshold. Buying one genuine endorsement costs an attacker roughly thirty dollars per identity.
